excluded_seen: The scale-up test's registered runs of this world: sides 512 and 1024 from starts 3001 to 3032, sides 2048 and 4096 from starts 4001 to 4016. They are what prompted this test: the side-2048 sample's live fraction at generation 1,000 was 0.04861 against 0.04827 at side 4096, five of their own standard errors apart.

The re-check (examples/scale-up-sizes/recheck.py): sixteen starts at side 2048, 5001 to 5016, which gave 0.04833. With them the gap between sides 2048 and 4096 is 0.0002, which is the margin registered here for the live fraction.

The laws at sides 32 to 256 from starts 2001 to 2032, the tie-break test and the first look (starts 101 to 228 and 9001 on). The spreads seen in all of these set the numbers of starts and the margins for the species balance and the mixing.
For timing, and to check the rented machine, a few generations at these sides from start 9001, and registered records of the scale-up test computed again.
No start of this test (6001 on) has been generated or run at any side.
body.interval: Welch's interval for the difference of two means, the smaller side minus the larger
body.statement: Life against HighLife under the standoff, from half-full mixed starts with equal shares on a wrapped square grid, at sides 1024, 2048 and 4096 from fresh starts. At generation 1,000 the three sides' means agree, pair by pair, within a margin: 0.0002 for the live fraction (the gap the scale-up test showed between sides 2048 and 4096), 0.0028 for species 1's share of the live cells and 0.00053 for the unlike share of adjacent live pairs.
body.title: Do the large grids agree with each other?
